domain_label: Document Ingestion & Chunking (Knowledge Distillation & Dense Representation subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is document extraction, cleaning, chunking, deduplication, serialization, and provenance capture
downstream embedding model and vector store are out of scope except as constraints on chunk size
primary document format is PDF; other formats handled via MULTI_FORMAT routing node
exclusions: image/audio modalities beyond figure caption extraction

glossary.definition: contiguous text span derived from a source document, annotated with position and provenance metadata, ready for embedding
correct sequential order of text blocks in a document accounting for multi-column layouts and sidebars
metadata recording the origin, extraction context, and transformation history of a chunk
one file partition in a set of JSONL files containing an approximately equal subset of chunks for parallel processing
two chunks with token Jaccard similarity above a threshold but not identical, often arising from boilerplate repetition
a chunk that belongs to a parent-child hierarchy, where child chunks are fine-grained and parent chunks provide context
a point in text where topic or theme shifts, detected via embedding similarity drop
identifier linking an ingested chunk to a structured knowledge base node for citation and retrieval traceability
fraction of source documents that produce non-empty extracted text, a key pipeline health metric

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for document ingestion and chunking work units in absence of supplied datasets

nodes.definition: Define the universe of input documents: file types (PDF, DOCX, HTML, plain text), source systems (S3, GCS, SharePoint, web crawl), access patterns, and volume estimates that drive subsequent extraction and chunking decisions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new document source type or storage system added

pros.claim: Prevents mid-pipeline format surprises by up-front enumeration
pros.example: discovering PPTX files after PDF pipeline is built

cons.claim: Incomplete inventory causes silent data gaps
cons.example: DOCX files excluded because inventory missed SharePoint mount

failure_modes: undiscovered file formats
unscoped volume growth exceeds pipeline capacity
acceptance_tests: all source systems enumerated with format distributions
volume estimates within 20% of actual

nodes.definition: Extract raw text, reading order, and structural annotations from PDFs using pdfplumber or PyMuPDF, handling multi-column layouts, scanned/OCR pages, embedded fonts, and ligature normalization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: PDF standard version or embedded-font type changes materially

pros.claim: pdfplumber preserves bounding boxes enabling coordinate-aware post-processing
pros.example: extracting table cells via bbox overlap

cons.claim: Scanned PDFs without OCR yield empty text silently

failure_modes: silent OCR skip on scanned pages
ligature splitting corrupting tokens
multi-column reading-order inversion
acceptance_tests: extracted text WER < 5% vs manual sample on scanned pages
reading order verified on multi-column fixture
no empty-string outputs without error flag

nodes.definition: Detect and classify document layout elements—headings, paragraphs, tables, figures, captions, headers/footers—using rule-based heuristics or ML layout models (LayoutLM, PaddleOCR) to enable structure-aware chunking.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new document template family or layout model version released

pros.claim: Preserves document hierarchy enabling section-aware chunking
pros.example: heading detection lets chunks respect section boundaries

cons.claim: ML layout models overfit to training document styles
cons.example: LayoutLM trained on scientific PDFs fails on legal briefs

failure_modes: header/footer content bleeding into body chunks
table misclassified as paragraph corrupting tabular data
acceptance_tests: element classification F1 > 0.85 on held-out fixture
headers/footers excluded from chunk text

nodes.definition: Extract table structure and cell content from detected table regions, converting to structured representations (JSON, Markdown) for downstream indexing, handling merged cells, multi-header rows, and nested tables.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: table format diversity in corpus increases

pros.claim: Preserves relational data otherwise lost as unstructured text
pros.example: financial tables with named columns stay queryable

cons.claim: Merged cells and nested tables cause cell boundary errors silently
cons.example: revenue table row span misaligned by 1 cell

failure_modes: merged-cell misassignment
multi-header row flattening losing semantics
acceptance_tests: cell content matches manual extraction on representative fixture
merged cells reconstructed without duplication

nodes.definition: Handle non-text content (charts, diagrams, photos) detected in documents: extract captions, generate alt-text via vision models if needed, decide whether to include image embeddings or caption-only representations in the ingestion pipeline.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: vision model capability improvements or policy changes on image data

pros.claim: Captures informational figures that drive downstream RAG quality
pros.example: chart caption included in chunk improves retrieval for visual queries

cons.claim: Vision alt-text generation adds latency and cost per page
cons.example: 1000-page PDF with 200 figures becomes expensive at $0.01/image

failure_modes: caption-figure association error
missing alt-text for informational figures
acceptance_tests: caption-figure association correct on fixture
alt-text generation pipeline toggleable without breaking downstream
revisit_triggers: figure density in corpus increases materially

nodes.definition: Choose and configure the chunking strategy—fixed-size with overlap, sentence-boundary, semantic/topic, or hierarchical—based on document type, embedding model context window, and downstream retrieval requirements.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: embedding model context window or retrieval architecture changes

pros.claim: Strategy choice is the single highest-leverage decision for downstream RAG recall/precision
pros.example: semantic chunking increases retrieval MRR by 15-25% vs fixed 512-token chunks

cons.claim: Wrong strategy is costly to redo once embeddings are indexed at scale
cons.example: switching from fixed to semantic requires full re-embed of 10M chunks

failure_modes: chunk size exceeding embedding model context window
no overlap causing split-sentence boundary losses
acceptance_tests: no chunk exceeds model token limit
retrieval recall@5 improves over fixed-256 baseline on eval set

nodes.definition: Split cleaned document text into fixed-token-count chunks with configurable overlap, respecting sentence boundaries where possible, and annotating chunk position metadata (doc_id, page, span).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: token budget or overlap policy changes

pros.claim: Simple, fast, and predictable; baseline for all chunk quality comparisons
pros.example: 256-token fixed chunks with 32-token overlap on Wikipedia corpus

cons.claim: Splits mid-sentence and mid-concept degrading retrieval quality
cons.example: answer sentence cut at chunk boundary misses retrieval

failure_modes: off-by-one overlap causing duplicate sentences
missing position metadata breaks provenance
acceptance_tests: no chunk exceeds token limit
overlap spans are contiguous with adjacent chunks
all chunks have doc_id and position metadata

nodes.definition: Segment documents at semantic topic boundaries detected via embedding similarity drops or topic model transitions, producing variable-length chunks that preserve semantic coherence at the cost of predictable size.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: embedding model or topic segmenter changes

pros.claim: Preserves topical coherence reducing split-concept retrieval failures
pros.example: scientific paper sections stay intact rather than mid-paragraph splits

cons.claim: Variable chunk sizes require size-guardrail logic to avoid oversized chunks
cons.example: topic-coherent passage 3x token limit crashes embedding model

failure_modes: all text classified as one topic producing single oversized chunk
boundary threshold too sensitive fragmenting paragraphs
acceptance_tests: chunk size distribution within [min_tokens, max_tokens] for >95% of chunks
intra-chunk semantic coherence score above threshold on eval set

nodes.definition: Construct a two-level chunk hierarchy: parent chunks (section-level) and child chunks (paragraph-level), linking them bidirectionally so retrieval can return a child chunk but expand to parent context for generation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: retrieval architecture changes to parent-child expansion pattern

pros.claim: Enables small-to-big retrieval: precise child match with full-section context
pros.example: retrieve paragraph, return section to LLM

cons.claim: Increases index complexity and requires parent-child id tracking
cons.example: orphaned child chunks if parent boundary logic errors

failure_modes: parent-child link broken by re-chunking
parent chunks exceeding LLM context window
acceptance_tests: every child chunk resolves to exactly one parent
parent context expansion tested end-to-end

nodes.definition: Clean extracted text by removing headers/footers/page-numbers, normalizing whitespace and Unicode, stripping boilerplate (disclaimers, navigation), fixing OCR artifacts, and applying language-consistent tokenization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: corpus language mix or boilerplate pattern changes

pros.claim: Removes noise that degrades embedding quality and retrieval precision
pros.example: stripping 'Page N of M' prevents spurious chunk matches on page numbers

cons.claim: Aggressive cleaning can remove legitimate content with similar patterns to boilerplate
cons.example: legal disclaimers legitimately needed for compliance chunks deleted

failure_modes: legitimate content deleted by over-aggressive boilerplate rules
encoding errors not caught leaving mojibake in chunks
acceptance_tests: headers/footers absent from 100% of test chunks
OCR artifact rate < 1% on sample
encoding validation passes all output text

nodes.definition: Detect and remove near-duplicate chunks or documents using MinHash/LSH, SimHash, or exact hash fingerprinting to avoid redundancy in the vector index that degrades retrieval diversity and wastes storage.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: corpus duplication rate changes or similarity threshold tuned

pros.claim: Prevents retrieval from surfacing N copies of the same passage
pros.example: annual report boilerplate deduplicated across 10 filing years

cons.claim: Aggressive Jaccard threshold removes legitimately similar but distinct chunks
cons.example: two paragraphs with same first 80% of tokens but different conclusions both deleted

failure_modes: threshold too low retaining near-duplicates
threshold too high removing distinct chunks
acceptance_tests: known duplicate pairs detected at >95% recall
distinct chunk pairs preserved at >98% precision

nodes.definition: Serialize deduplicated chunks with provenance metadata (doc_id, chunk_id, source, page, section, chunk_type) to sharded JSONL files sized for parallel embedding ingestion, with manifest tracking total chunk counts and shard checksums.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: downstream embedding pipeline batch size or storage format changes

pros.claim: Sharded JSONL enables embarrassingly parallel embedding at scale
pros.example: 100 shards processed on 100 workers in 1/100th the time

cons.claim: Missing provenance fields break downstream node-id mapping silently
cons.example: chunk_id absent means no lineage from vector hit to source document

failure_modes: incomplete provenance schema
shard manifest checksum mismatch
acceptance_tests: all chunks contain required provenance fields
manifest chunk count matches sum of shard counts
checksum validates all shards

nodes.definition: Map each ingested chunk to its corresponding downstream KB node identifier, enabling traceability from vector-search hits back to structured knowledge graph nodes, using document section labels and taxonomy mappings.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: KB node taxonomy or document section label schema changes

pros.claim: Enables RAG pipelines to attribute retrieved text to specific KB nodes for citation
pros.example: chunk from section 3.2 maps to KB node PROC_007 enabling structured citation

cons.claim: Taxonomy misalignment causes node-id gaps that silently break downstream citation
cons.example: section heading rename breaks all mappings relying on string match

failure_modes: unmapped chunks silently excluded from KB
taxonomy mismatch causing wrong node assignment
acceptance_tests: mapping coverage > 95% of chunks
spot-check node assignments correct on 50-chunk sample

nodes.definition: Record full lineage for every chunk: source document URI, extraction timestamp, extractor version, page/section coordinates, chunk sequence index, and parent chunk id, persisting to a provenance store for audit and reproducibility.

pros.claim: Full chunk provenance enables debugging retrieval failures back to source
pros.example: wrong answer traced to incorrectly OCR'd page 47 of document X version 2023-03

cons.claim: Provenance store size grows linearly with chunk count
cons.example: 10M chunks at 500 bytes provenance each = 5GB overhead

failure_modes: extractor version not pinned causing irreproducibility
provenance store not kept in sync with chunk store
acceptance_tests: every chunk resolvable to source URI via provenance
extractor version recorded for all chunks
provenance store transactionally consistent with chunk store

nodes.definition: Validate that the final chunk JSONL meets embedding pipeline prerequisites: token-count within model limit, required fields present, encoding valid UTF-8, no empty text, and shard checksums verified before handing off to the embedding stage.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: embedding model or field schema changes

pros.claim: Catches schema and token-limit violations before expensive embedding run
pros.example: saves 2hr GPU time by catching 50 oversized chunks before embedding batch

cons.claim: Validation adds latency before embedding starts
cons.example: strict validation delays pipeline start by 15min for large shards

failure_modes: token limit check using wrong tokenizer
silent pass on empty text fields
acceptance_tests: zero oversized chunks pass validation
validation correctly rejects known-invalid fixture
go/no-go signal blocks embedding on any critical failure
revisit_triggers: embedding model swap changes token limits

nodes.definition: Instrument the ingestion pipeline with metrics (extraction yield, chunk count per doc, dedup rate, error rate, latency per stage) and alerting to detect anomalies such as extraction failures, unexpected chunk size distributions, or throughput degradation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pipeline SLA or alert threshold changes

pros.claim: Proactive anomaly detection prevents silent data quality degradation
pros.example: alert fires when extraction yield drops 20%, catching PDF library regression

cons.claim: Monitoring overhead adds per-chunk latency if metrics are synchronously emitted
cons.example: synchronous metric emission doubles single-threaded ingest time

failure_modes: silent extraction failure uncaught without yield monitoring
alert thresholds set too loose missing gradual degradation
acceptance_tests: extraction yield metric captured per document
alert fires within 5min of simulated failure injection
dashboard latency metric accurate within 10%

nodes.definition: Implement incremental ingestion of new or updated source documents by detecting changes via content hash or modification timestamp, re-ingesting only changed documents, invalidating stale chunks in the vector store, and updating provenance.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: document update frequency or vector store invalidation SLA changes

pros.claim: Reduces ingestion cost from full-corpus to only changed documents
pros.example: daily incremental runs 10x faster than full reindex for 1% change rate

cons.claim: Stale chunk invalidation logic is complex and error-prone
cons.example: renamed section heading causes old chunks to persist alongside new ones

failure_modes: stale chunks not invalidated causing outdated retrieval
change detection missing update due to metadata-only change
acceptance_tests: updated document re-indexed within pipeline SLA
stale chunks removed from vector store after update
unchanged documents not re-processed

nodes.definition: Route non-PDF document formats (DOCX, HTML, Markdown, EPUB, plain text) to format-specific extractors, normalize outputs to a common text-plus-structure schema, and merge into the unified ingestion pipeline.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new document format added to source inventory

pros.claim: Single schema for all formats simplifies downstream chunking and embedding
pros.example: DOCX policy documents and HTML web pages chunked by same pipeline

cons.claim: Each new format adds maintenance surface and version-dependency risk
cons.example: python-docx incompatible with DOCX 2024 format requires library update

failure_modes: unsupported format silently producing empty extraction
format detection misrouting binary file as text
acceptance_tests: all enumerated formats produce non-empty normalized output
format detection correctly routes 100% of test fixture files
revisit_triggers: new format added to source inventory

nodes.definition: Evaluate chunk quality using automated metrics (coherence score, token length distribution, boundary quality, information density) and a small human-annotated eval set to identify and fix systematic chunking defects before full-scale indexing.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: chunking strategy changes or retrieval quality regression

pros.claim: Early defect detection prevents propagating chunking errors through expensive embedding stage
pros.example: discovering mid-sentence split defect before 10M-chunk embedding run

cons.claim: Human annotation is costly; automated metrics imperfect proxies
cons.example: coherence score doesn't catch factual boundary errors

failure_modes: eval set too small to surface systematic defects
automated metrics miss domain-specific quality issues
acceptance_tests: chunk coherence score above baseline threshold on eval set
token distribution within expected range
human annotation agreement > 80%

edges.why_related: PDF extraction scope is defined by source plan
edges.benefit_of_coupling: ensures PDF extractor covers all PDF source types
edges.risk_of_conflict: source plan missing PDF variants causes extraction gaps
edges.example: watermarked PDFs discovered post-pipeline build
edges.resolution_rule: source plan dominates; update extractor when new PDF type added

edges.why_related: multi-format router handles formats enumerated in source plan
edges.benefit_of_coupling: router covers exactly the format inventory
edges.risk_of_conflict: unlisted format silently fails
edges.example: EPUB format missed in plan, router has no EPUB handler
edges.resolution_rule: source plan is authoritative; router updated for each new format

edges.why_related: chunk strategy depends on document type mix from source plan
edges.benefit_of_coupling: strategy choice informed by format and length distribution
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong strategy for format mix degrades retrieval
edges.example: long-form books need hierarchical chunking discovered post-strategy lock
edges.resolution_rule: source plan must be finalized before chunk strategy

edges.why_related: cleaning operates on raw extracted text
edges.benefit_of_coupling: cleaning removes PDF extraction artifacts systematically
edges.risk_of_conflict: uncleaned extraction text degrades downstream quality
edges.example: page numbers in extracted text propagate to chunks
edges.resolution_rule: extraction always precedes cleaning

edges.why_related: layout detection uses bounding box metadata from PDF extractor
edges.benefit_of_coupling: extractor provides coordinates layout model needs
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing bboxes break rule-based layout detection
edges.example: PyMuPDF bbox data required by LayoutLM preprocessing
edges.resolution_rule: extraction and layout must use compatible coordinate systems

edges.why_related: table extraction operates on table regions detected by layout model
edges.benefit_of_coupling: layout detection localizes tables reducing extraction search space
edges.risk_of_conflict: layout miss causes table extraction to miss tables
edges.example: table bboxes from layout feed cell extraction logic
edges.resolution_rule: layout detection must complete before table extraction

edges.why_related: figure handling operates on figure regions from layout detection
edges.benefit_of_coupling: layout localizes figures for caption extraction
edges.risk_of_conflict: layout miss causes figure captions to be lost
edges.example: figure bbox from layout used to find adjacent caption text
edges.resolution_rule: layout detection must complete before figure handling

edges.why_related: hierarchical chunking uses section boundaries from layout detection
edges.benefit_of_coupling: section hierarchy from layout enables correct parent chunk boundaries
edges.risk_of_conflict: without layout hierarchy chunking produces flat wrong parent boundaries
edges.example: H1/H2 section labels from layout define parent chunk breaks
edges.resolution_rule: layout detection must be run before hierarchical chunking

edges.why_related: fixed chunking operates on cleaned normalized text
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clean text reduces junk token pollution in chunks
edges.risk_of_conflict: uncleaned text produces polluted chunks
edges.example: page-number tokens removed before chunk token counting
edges.resolution_rule: cleaning always precedes chunking

edges.why_related: semantic chunking requires clean text for coherent embedding similarity
edges.benefit_of_coupling: noise removal improves similarity signal for boundary detection
edges.risk_of_conflict: noisy text creates false similarity drops misplacing chunk boundaries
edges.example: OCR artifacts produce spurious low-similarity points
edges.resolution_rule: cleaning always precedes semantic chunking

edges.why_related: fixed chunking is one concrete strategy choice
edges.benefit_of_coupling: strategy config drives fixed chunk size and overlap params
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong size/overlap from bad strategy degrades retrieval
edges.example: 256-token fixed strategy config passed to fixed chunker
edges.resolution_rule: strategy selection precedes chunker execution

edges.why_related: semantic chunking is one concrete strategy choice
edges.benefit_of_coupling: strategy config drives similarity threshold and min/max sizes
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong threshold from bad strategy produces oversized chunks
edges.example: semantic strategy selects cosine-threshold=0.85
edges.resolution_rule: strategy selection precedes chunker execution

edges.why_related: hierarchical chunking is one concrete strategy choice
edges.benefit_of_coupling: strategy config defines parent and child size targets
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong parent size creates chunks exceeding LLM context
edges.example: hierarchical strategy: parent=2048 tokens, child=256 tokens
edges.resolution_rule: strategy selection precedes chunker execution

edges.why_related: dedup operates on fixed chunks to remove near-duplicates
edges.benefit_of_coupling: dedup reduces redundancy in fixed-chunk output
edges.risk_of_conflict: without dedup duplicate annual report boilerplate inflates index
edges.example: MinHash applied to fixed chunk token sets
edges.resolution_rule: chunking always precedes deduplication

edges.why_related: dedup operates on semantic chunks to remove near-duplicates
edges.benefit_of_coupling: dedup catches same-topic passages chunked from different documents
edges.risk_of_conflict: without dedup near-identical passages from mirrored sites inflate index
edges.example: SimHash on semantic chunk text
edges.resolution_rule: chunking always precedes deduplication

edges.why_related: dedup operates on child chunks from hierarchical chunking
edges.benefit_of_coupling: dedup prevents duplicate child chunks from overlapping source sections
edges.risk_of_conflict: without dedup parent-spanning duplicates from OCR variants appear
edges.example: exact hash dedup on child chunk text
edges.resolution_rule: chunking always precedes deduplication

edges.why_related: JSONL sharding operates on deduplicated chunk list
edges.benefit_of_coupling: dedup before sharding ensures clean shard content
edges.risk_of_conflict: sharding before dedup propagates duplicates to all downstream
edges.example: deduplicated chunk list serialized to 100-shard JSONL
edges.resolution_rule: deduplication always precedes sharding

edges.why_related: node mapping enriches JSONL shards with KB node ids
edges.benefit_of_coupling: provenance fields in JSONL enable mapping resolution
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing section labels in JSONL break node mapping
edges.example: section_label field from JSONL matched to KB taxonomy
edges.resolution_rule: JSONL sharding precedes node mapping enrichment

edges.why_related: provenance capture records lineage from sharded JSONL
edges.benefit_of_coupling: JSONL schema includes all provenance fields needed
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing fields in JSONL break provenance store
edges.example: source_uri and chunk_id in JSONL required for provenance
edges.resolution_rule: JSONL schema must include provenance fields before capture runs

edges.why_related: embedding readiness check validates node-mapped JSONL
edges.benefit_of_coupling: validation confirms node_id field present in final JSONL
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing node_id field causes validation failure
edges.example: embed-ready check confirms kb_node_id field non-null
edges.resolution_rule: node mapping precedes embedding readiness validation

edges.why_related: embedding readiness validates provenance completeness
edges.benefit_of_coupling: validation catches missing provenance before embedding
edges.risk_of_conflict: incomplete provenance passes through to embedding silently
edges.example: source_uri presence check in embed-ready validation
edges.resolution_rule: provenance capture precedes embedding readiness gate

edges.why_related: incremental ingest reuses the same embed-ready validation gate
edges.benefit_of_coupling: validation gate shared between full and incremental pipelines
edges.risk_of_conflict: incremental chunks bypassing validation introduce bad data
edges.example: delta JSONL from incremental also passes embed-ready gate
edges.resolution_rule: embed-ready validation must also gate incremental pipeline

edges.why_related: extraction yield metric is key pipeline health signal
edges.benefit_of_coupling: monitoring catches PDF extraction failures early
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmonitored extraction failures cause silent data gaps
edges.example: yield alert fires when extraction produces zero text for a document
edges.resolution_rule: monitoring must be instrumented at extraction stage

edges.why_related: dedup rate metric indicates corpus duplication health
edges.benefit_of_coupling: monitoring dedup rate detects corpora anomalies
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmonitored dedup rate hides data quality issues
edges.example: dedup rate spike alert indicates corpus mirror was added
edges.resolution_rule: monitoring tracks dedup rate as a data health signal

edges.why_related: incremental ingest uses provenance to detect changed documents
edges.benefit_of_coupling: provenance enables efficient change detection by hash comparison
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing provenance forces full reindex on updates
edges.example: content hash from provenance compared to detect updates
edges.resolution_rule: provenance must be current for incremental to work correctly

edges.why_related: chunk quality evaluation is grounded in strategy choice
edges.benefit_of_coupling: quality eval validates that chosen strategy meets quality targets
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong strategy discovered too late after full embedding run
edges.example: quality eval on 1000-chunk sample before full pipeline run
edges.resolution_rule: chunk quality evaluation gates strategy finalization

edges.why_related: embed-ready check follows chunk quality approval
edges.benefit_of_coupling: quality gate precedes final embedding readiness validation
edges.risk_of_conflict: embedding run before quality check propagates defects at scale
edges.example: quality report go-signal required before embed-ready check
edges.resolution_rule: chunk quality evaluation precedes embedding readiness gate

edges.why_related: multi-format output feeds same cleaning stage as PDF
edges.benefit_of_coupling: unified cleaning handles artifacts from all extractors
edges.risk_of_conflict: format-specific artifacts not cleaned degrade chunk quality
edges.example: DOCX tracked-change markup cleaned same as PDF artifacts
edges.resolution_rule: all format extractors feed into unified cleaning stage

edges.why_related: non-PDF formats have partial layout information needing normalization
edges.benefit_of_coupling: layout detection normalizes structure across formats
edges.risk_of_conflict: HTML heading tags and DOCX styles both map to section hierarchy
edges.example: H1-H6 from HTML normalized to same section hierarchy as PDF headings
edges.resolution_rule: layout detection must handle non-PDF structural signals

edges.why_related: quality failure may require strategy revision creating a conflict
edges.benefit_of_coupling: quality feedback loop improves strategy selection
edges.risk_of_conflict: quality failure requiring strategy revision causes full re-chunk rework
edges.example: semantic chunking quality failure forces switch to hierarchical strategy
edges.resolution_rule: if quality fails: re-evaluate strategy before re-chunking

edges.why_related: semantic and fixed chunking are mutually exclusive strategy choices
edges.benefit_of_coupling: one chunk type per pipeline run avoids mixed indexing
edges.risk_of_conflict: mixing chunk types in same index causes inconsistent retrieval
edges.example: semantic chunks in same FAISS index as fixed chunks degrade recall
edges.resolution_rule: strategy selection must commit to one chunk type before pipeline run

edges.why_related: table-heavy corpus requires table-aware chunking strategy
edges.benefit_of_coupling: table content informs strategy to avoid splitting mid-table
edges.risk_of_conflict: table rows split across chunk boundaries corrupt tabular retrieval
edges.example: strategy uses table fraction in corpus to select table-boundary chunking
edges.resolution_rule: table extraction results inform strategy configuration

edges.why_related: incremental ingestion generates same metrics as full ingestion
edges.benefit_of_coupling: monitoring covers incremental pipeline for anomaly detection
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmonitored incremental runs miss stale-chunk invalidation failures
edges.example: incremental yield metric alerts on document update processing failures
edges.resolution_rule: monitoring must be instrumented for incremental pipeline too

edges.why_related: table extraction depends on page content from PDF extractor
edges.benefit_of_coupling: PDF extractor provides text and bbox needed for cell extraction
edges.risk_of_conflict: PDF extraction quality directly limits table extraction accuracy
edges.example: cell position extraction depends on pdfplumber coordinate output
edges.resolution_rule: PDF extraction quality gates table extraction quality

edges.why_related: figure metadata and captions serialized into JSONL
edges.benefit_of_coupling: figure captions included in JSONL improve multimodal retrieval
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing figure records cause gaps in multimodal index
edges.example: figure caption and alt-text fields added to JSONL record
edges.resolution_rule: figure handling output serialized alongside text chunks

edges.why_related: incremental ingest scope defined by document source inventory
edges.benefit_of_coupling: source plan defines which systems support change detection
edges.risk_of_conflict: systems without modification timestamps cannot support incremental ingest
edges.example: S3 versioning enables hash-based change detection per source plan
edges.resolution_rule: incremental ingest feasibility determined by source plan system capabilities

conflict_axes.description: Fixed-size chunks are predictable and cheap but split concepts; semantic chunks preserve coherence but have variable size and higher cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: select based on embedding model context window and retrieval latency budget; use semantic for long-form domain docs, fixed for short homogeneous text

conflict_axes.description: Full OCR+layout extraction maximizes text yield but is slow; fast text-only extraction is cheap but misses scanned pages and structure
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use OCR+layout for knowledge-critical PDFs; fast extraction for high-volume low-criticality text

conflict_axes.description: Full chunk provenance enables audit and debugging but grows linearly with chunk count
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: capture full provenance but compress; index by doc_id and chunk_id to minimize storage

conflict_axes.description: Aggressive dedup removes near-duplicates improving index efficiency but risks removing distinct similar chunks
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tune Jaccard threshold on a labeled corpus sample; prefer recall over precision for knowledge-critical content

conflict_axes.description: Hierarchical chunking enables parent-context expansion but adds index complexity and parent-child link maintenance cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use hierarchical for document-centric QA; use flat for snippet-level retrieval

conflict_axes.description: Full reindex guarantees consistency but is expensive; incremental ingest is cheap but risks stale chunk accumulation
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use incremental for <20% daily change rate; schedule periodic full reindex to eliminate stale chunk drift

conflict_axes.description: Supporting many formats maximizes corpus coverage but each format adds an extractor dependency to maintain
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prioritize formats by corpus volume share; maintain extractors for formats covering >5% of corpus

conflict_axes.description: Human-annotated chunk quality evaluation is expensive but automated metrics miss domain defects; skipping evaluation risks propagating chunking defects to full embedding run
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always run automated metrics; do human annotation for new document domains or after strategy changes

conflict_axes.description: Serializing tables as markdown text enables unified text index but loses table structure; structured JSON table index preserves structure but requires separate retrieval path
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use markdown text serialization for QA; add structured index only if table-specific queries are a primary use case

edge_cases.title: scanned_pdf_with_no_text_layer
edge_cases.description: PDF contains only images with no embedded text layer; text extraction returns empty string without error
edge_cases.recommended_action: detect zero-yield pages; route to OCR pipeline; alert if OCR also fails

edge_cases.title: multilingual_document_with_mixed_scripts
edge_cases.description: Document contains mixed-language text (e.g. English headers with Arabic body); single-language tokenizer corrupts token counts for non-Latin scripts
edge_cases.trigger_condition: character set analysis detects multi-script in same document
edge_cases.recommended_action: apply language detection per paragraph; use multilingual tokenizer for token-count chunking

edge_cases.title: extremely_large_table_spanning_multiple_pages
edge_cases.description: Table spans 10+ pages; naive page-by-page extraction treats each page as a separate table losing row continuity
edge_cases.trigger_condition: table region detected at bottom of page with continuation on next page
edge_cases.recommended_action: implement table continuation detection using column header repetition as signal

edge_cases.title: chunk_exceeds_embedding_model_context_window
edge_cases.description: Semantic chunker produces a single oversized chunk when entire document is topically coherent
edge_cases.trigger_condition: semantic similarity never drops below threshold producing one chunk
edge_cases.recommended_action: enforce max-token hard limit; split at sentence boundary when limit exceeded

edge_cases.title: near_duplicate_with_factual_difference
edge_cases.description: Two chunks share 90% token overlap but differ in a key date or figure; aggressive dedup removes the factually distinct chunk
edge_cases.trigger_condition: Jaccard similarity above threshold but content differs in named entities
edge_cases.recommended_action: add named-entity preservation check before dedup deletion; lower threshold for entity-dense chunks

edge_cases.title: header_footer_content_mistaken_for_body
edge_cases.description: Unusual document template places recurring section title in position that appears as body text; cleaning rule removes legitimate heading
edge_cases.trigger_condition: cleaning rule triggers on text that passes positional check
edge_cases.recommended_action: layout detection should classify before cleaning; cleaning should operate on layout-classified body text only

edge_cases.title: document_update_with_same_filename_different_content
edge_cases.description: Source document updated silently (no timestamp change) causing incremental ingest to miss re-indexing; stale chunks persist
edge_cases.trigger_condition: modification timestamp unchanged but content hash differs
edge_cases.recommended_action: use content hash as primary change signal not timestamp; always compare content hash regardless of timestamp

edge_cases.title: figure_caption_farther_than_proximity_threshold
edge_cases.description: Figure caption is located 3 pages after the figure due to document layout; proximity-based caption extraction associates wrong text as caption
edge_cases.trigger_condition: caption not within N pixels/lines of figure bbox
edge_cases.recommended_action: use document structure signals (caption tag, style) in addition to proximity; allow null caption with warning

edge_cases.title: kb_node_id_taxonomy_version_mismatch
edge_cases.description: Chunk node mapping uses old taxonomy version while KB graph has been updated; chunks map to deprecated or nonexistent node ids
edge_cases.trigger_condition: node id lookup fails for >5% of chunks
edge_cases.recommended_action: pin taxonomy version in chunk node mapping config; validate all node ids against current KB on each run

edge_cases.title: zero_byte_file_in_source_inventory
edge_cases.description: Source document is empty (zero bytes) or corrupted; extractor raises no error but yields empty text causing chunk count = 0
edge_cases.trigger_condition: file size = 0 or extraction yields 0 text
edge_cases.recommended_action: pre-flight file validation step; alert and log zero-byte files before extraction; skip gracefully

edge_cases.title: encoding_mojibake_in_extracted_text
edge_cases.description: PDF font encoding mismatch causes garbled Unicode characters in extracted text that pass UTF-8 validity but are semantically wrong
edge_cases.trigger_condition: character n-gram distribution anomaly detected in extracted text
edge_cases.recommended_action: apply character-level language model perplexity check on extracted text sample; flag high-perplexity outputs for review

edge_cases.title: parallel_column_text_merged_incorrectly
edge_cases.description: Two-column layout PDF has text from both columns interleaved in reading order producing nonsensical sentences
edge_cases.trigger_condition: reading order quality check detects sentence incoherence
edge_cases.recommended_action: use column detection from layout model before reading-order reconstruction; process columns separately then merge

workflow.name: source_inventory
workflow.description: Enumerate all document sources, formats, and volumes; produce source manifest
workflow.on_failure: add missing format handlers before proceeding

workflow.name: extraction
workflow.description: Run PDF and multi-format extractors; collect reading-order text and bboxes
workflow.on_failure: diagnose OCR failures; fix encoding issues

workflow.name: layout_detection
workflow.description: Run layout model to classify elements; build section hierarchy

workflow.name: table_and_figure_extraction
workflow.description: Extract table structure and figure captions from detected regions

workflow.name: text_cleaning
workflow.description: Clean extracted text; remove boilerplate, normalize encoding
workflow.decision_gate: boilerplate removal rate >= 99% and no legitimate content lost

workflow.name: chunk_strategy_and_quality
workflow.description: Select chunking strategy; run sample evaluation before full pipeline

workflow.name: chunking
workflow.description: Execute selected chunking strategy (fixed, semantic, or hierarchical)
workflow.decision_gate: no chunk exceeds token limit; position metadata complete

workflow.name: deduplication
workflow.description: Apply MinHash/LSH dedup to remove near-duplicate chunks

workflow.name: serialization_and_provenance
workflow.description: Serialize to sharded JSONL; capture provenance; map to KB node ids
workflow.decision_gate: manifest counts match; provenance complete; mapping coverage >= 95%

workflow.name: embedding_readiness_validation
workflow.description: Validate final JSONL against embedding pipeline prerequisites

workflow.name: pipeline_monitoring_and_incremental
workflow.description: Operate monitoring and incremental update pipeline for ongoing ingestion
workflow.decision_gate: no unresolved alerts; incremental yield normal
workflow.on_failure: investigate anomaly; escalate to full reindex if needed

dominance_rules.description: No chunk may exceed the embedding model's context window; this constraint dominates all other chunk size preferences
dominance_rules.dominated_concern: preferred semantic coherence at expense of size

dominance_rules.description: Content hash is the authoritative change signal for incremental ingest; timestamp is a secondary signal only
dominance_rules.dominated_concern: modification timestamp as primary change signal

dominance_rules.description: The sequence extraction -> cleaning -> chunking is invariant; no stage may be reordered
dominance_rules.dominated_concern: performance shortcuts that skip cleaning before chunking

dominance_rules.description: Every output chunk must have doc_id, chunk_id, source_uri, and page metadata; provenance is non-optional
dominance_rules.dominated_concern: omitting provenance to reduce record size

dominance_rules.description: Document source inventory must be complete before investing in extractor code; format surprises post-build are expensive
Chunk quality evaluation on a sample must pass before full corpus chunking and embedding; avoids expensive propagation of systematic defects
dominance_rules.dominated_concern: skipping sample quality eval to save time

dominance_rules.description: Section hierarchy from layout detection is a prerequisite for hierarchical and semantic chunking; layout cannot be added post-hoc
dominance_rules.dominated_concern: chunking first then trying to add layout

dominance_rules.description: Deduplication must run before JSONL serialization; deduplicating post-serialization requires re-serializing all shards
KB node id mapping must use the current KB taxonomy version; stale mapping silently produces invalid node references
Incremental ingestion accumulates stale chunk drift; a scheduled full reindex is required to maintain consistency
dominance_rules.dominated_concern: running incremental indefinitely without full reindex

anti_rework_rules.rationale: Extractor rewrites for undiscovered formats waste engineering time
anti_rework_rules.do_not_do: start coding extractors before source plan complete
anti_rework_rules.instead_do: finalize source manifest; then build extractors

anti_rework_rules.rationale: Propagating chunking defects to full embedding run is expensive and slow to diagnose
anti_rework_rules.do_not_do: run full pipeline then check quality
anti_rework_rules.instead_do: evaluate on 1000-chunk sample; fix strategy; then run full

anti_rework_rules.rationale: Chunk strategy change requires full re-embed; lock strategy before any embedding
anti_rework_rules.do_not_do: change chunk size during embedding run

anti_rework_rules.rationale: Extractor library updates change output silently; unpinned versions cause non-reproducible extraction
anti_rework_rules.do_not_do: use floating version constraints for pdfplumber/PyMuPDF
anti_rework_rules.instead_do: pin exact versions in requirements.txt and provenance record

anti_rework_rules.rationale: Adding provenance fields post-serialization requires re-running all serialization and re-embedding
anti_rework_rules.do_not_do: serialize chunks then discover missing provenance fields
anti_rework_rules.instead_do: define and validate provenance schema before first serialization run

anti_rework_rules.rationale: Domain mismatch in layout model causes systematic element misclassification across all documents
anti_rework_rules.do_not_do: use scientific PDF layout model on legal documents without validation
anti_rework_rules.instead_do: validate layout model F1 on 50-document sample from target domain

anti_rework_rules.rationale: Stale chunk accumulation from broken invalidation degrades retrieval silently
anti_rework_rules.do_not_do: disable full reindex before validating incremental invalidation correctness
anti_rework_rules.instead_do: test stale chunk invalidation on update fixture before relying on incremental

anti_rework_rules.rationale: Dedup after node mapping may delete a chunk whose node mapping partner is retained, breaking citation integrity
anti_rework_rules.instead_do: dedup before node mapping; mapping runs on clean deduplicated set

anti_rework_rules.rationale: Silent OCR failure on scanned pages causes empty chunks that pass format validation
anti_rework_rules.do_not_do: trust extraction yield without per-document OCR validation
anti_rework_rules.instead_do: validate extraction yield per document; alert on zero-text documents

iteration_protocol.action: investigate per-document extraction errors; check OCR pipeline; review source format changes
re-evaluate chunking strategy; run CHUNK_QUALITY on sample; revise strategy if needed
reconfigure CHUNK_STRATEGY for new context window; re-run EMBED_READY validation; re-embed all shards
update DOC_SOURCE_PLAN; add format handler to MULTI_FORMAT; re-run ingestion for new format documents
re-run CHUNK_NODE_MAP with new taxonomy; validate mapping coverage; update provenance records
investigate corpus duplication source; adjust threshold if corpus characteristics changed; re-run DEDUP
investigate invalidation logic; schedule full reindex if stale accumulation exceeds threshold
re-validate layout model on current document sample; fine-tune or switch model if error rate persists
diagnose missing provenance fields; re-serialize affected chunks with correct provenance schema

priority_rationale: DOC_SOURCE_PLAN anchors all format scope; PDF_EXTRACT is the highest-volume extraction path; CLEAN_NORM is universal prerequisite to chunking quality; LAYOUT_DETECT unlocks structure-aware chunking; CHUNK_STRATEGY is highest-leverage design decision; EMBED_READY gates the expensive embedding run; PROV_CAPTURE is non-negotiable for audit; SHARD_JSONL enables parallel embedding; DEDUP improves index quality; CHUNK_QUALITY validates strategy; chunkers ranked by complexity: FIXED < SEM < TABLE_EXTRACT = MULTI_FORMAT < HIER_CHUNK; CHUNK_NODE_MAP and INCR_INGEST support ongoing operations; INGEST_MONITOR provides observability; FIGURE_HANDLE is supplementary.

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHUNK_STRATEGY, FIXED_CHUNK, SEM_CHUNK, HIER_CHUNK define options

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEM_CHUNK vs FIXED_CHUNK conflict edge and definitions
